land.text: the Katsina country round Birnin Katsina (the page gives no outline)

successors.note: Conquered in the jihad of Usman dan Fodio in 1805/6 (Umaru Dallaji killed Sarkin Katsina Mare Mawa Mahmudu at Sabon Birni; Halidu killed himself); "The remainder of the exiled Katsinawa went further north and founded the city of Maradi". The British deposed Sarkin Katsina Abubakar of the Dallazawa line in 1904.

capitals.name: Birnin Katsina
capitals.note: Infobox: "Birnin Katsina, the capital of Katsina"; Muhammadu Korau (c. 1445-1495) is credited with the walled settlement. Coordinates approximate.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Katsina row). The regnal list dates the first dynasty (Kumayo) to 1015 CE; the infobox says "early second millennium CE" (1100 to the 15th century). No area on the page; the Katsina State stands for the core. Songhai made Katsina a vassal in 1512 (to 1554) and Katsina later allied with Bornu and paid tribute to Zaria (1576-1610): tributary ties, not drawn.

ledger.note: 1015: the Kumayo dynasty founds Katsina. "The first dynasty to rule over Katsina was established by Kumayo"; the regnal list dates it to 1015 CE, the infobox to "the early second millennium CE".

region.text: the Katsina country round Birnin Katsina (the page gives no outline)

ledger.note: 1512: Songhai conquers Katsina. "Askia Muhammad conquered Katsina in 1512" and Katsina became a vassal of Gao; it "regained its independence in 1554" after the battle of Karfata.

region.text: the Katsina country round Birnin Katsina (the page gives no outline)

ledger.note: 1554: Katsina regains its independence from Songhai after the battle of Karfata.

region.text: the Katsina country round Birnin Katsina (the page gives no outline)

ledger.note: 1805/6: the Fulani take Katsina. Umaru Dallaji killed Sarkin Katsina Mare Mawa Mahmudu at Sabon Birni; Sarkin Katsina Halidu killed himself by throwing himself down a well, which ended the Korau dynasty. The Sokoto dossier dates the gain to 1807.

region.text: the Katsina country round Birnin Katsina (the page gives no outline)

ledger.note: 1806: the Hausa state of Katsina ends; its surviving ruling house founds Maradi to the north.

wars.name: Songhai conquest of Katsina

zones.text: the Katsina country round Birnin Katsina (the page gives no outline)

wars.outcome: Askia Muhammad conquered Katsina in 1512 and it was a vassal of Gao until it regained independence in 1554 (battle of Karfata).
wars.note: Mapped as an occupation by Songhai; the songhai-empire dossier carries the matching tribute relation as a gap.

wars.name: Kano-Katsina wars
wars.outcome: The eleven-year war under Rumfa "remained indecisive"; Kano later defeated Katsina under Abdullahi; in the 1570s "Katsina launched an attack" that reached Kano's gates; around 1671 Kwararafa also invaded Katsina and breached its walls.

wars.outcome: The Fulani under Umaru Dallaji conquered Katsina in 1805/6; the Korau dynasty ended.

certainty.note: No frontier on the page; the Hausa state was a walled city with a plain, its tributaries (Songhai 1512-1554, Bornu from the late 16th century, Zaria 1576-1610) are not drawn.

sources.title: Katsina Emirate
sources.note: Identity, regnal list 1015, Korau c. 1445-1495, Songhai 1512-1554, Bornu allegiance, Fulani conquest 1805/6, Maradi, British 1904; no area.

notes:
Sultanate of Katsina (Katsina Emirate before 1806), additions batch af-03-x; Cliopatria has no row. Page: Katsina Emirate (1 page).

Dates: founding 1015 (regnal list) versus "early second millennium" (infobox 1100 to the 15th century): 1015 is a confidence-1 anchor; end 1805/6 (this page) versus 1807 (Sokoto dossier's reading of the Sokoto page); Songhai's conquest 1512 and independence 1554 are on this page only and are not in the songhai-empire dossier (which lists Askia-era Hausaland conquests as a gap): that dossier should carry vassal_start 1512 and vassal_end 1554 for katsina. Not on the page: an area or frontier; Kebbi, Gobir and Daura conquests; Bornu's tribute details (one hundred slaves per accession). The exile at Maradi (Katsina-Maradi, Niger) continues after 1806 and needs a dossier. Gazetteer: Birnin Katsina (place Katsina exists), Maradi (admin1 exists).
